<thought>Based on the observed isotopic pattern—a strong monoisotopic peak at m/z 183, a clear M+2 peak at m/z 185 with roughly one‑third the intensity of the base peak (consistent with the ~3:1 natural abundance of ^35Cl/^37Cl)—chlorine can be definitively identified. No other element shows a characteristic isotopic signature (e.g., the ~1:1 M/M+2 of bromine or the very low‑intensity M+2 of sulfur). Therefore, the only element that can be definitively identified from the spectrum is chlorine.</thought>
<final_answer>['Cl']</final_answer>
